summary: Root joined all accepted artifacts and passed the materializer, full fixture, JSON, fault-gate, preservation, fingerprint, policy, and dirty-state checks. Remaining concerns are bounded historical/live-version distinctions and route attestation limits, not failed acceptance gates.

claims.claim: The isolated write-producing DAG passes all deterministic implementation and integration tests.
The pre-existing user dirty edit was preserved byte-for-byte and the named-run working state contains exactly the accepted paths.
evidence: Exact seven-path git status assertion passed.

claims.claim: The required fault gates all behaved fail closed and recovered only through explicit lifecycle changes.
evidence: F1 overlapping write scope and resource lock were rejected before dispatch with zero workers.
F2 revision 1 returned NEEDS_CONTEXT; revision 2 supplied the required artifact and returned DONE.
T2/T3/T4 stale revisions and T4 revision 1 BLOCKED evidence were preserved while descendants were replanned.
F3 unavailable effort tier remains requested and unattested with no worker or receipt.
T4 revision 2 resolved the ordering contradiction through the sole generated-output owner.

claims.claim: The v0.1 evidence archive and immutable snapshot remain intact, and both fingerprint interpretations reproduce.
The only live-vs-v0.1 Skill delta is the intentional TaskContract policy amendment recorded by ADR-0003.
evidence: Six of seven live files still match the immutable snapshot.

uncertainty: The historical fingerprint label remains immutable and must be read with ADR-0002: 856358... is OrdinalIgnoreCase/manifest order; 11B134... is true case-sensitive Ordinal.
The root execution route is observed but the exact root model/effort is inherited-unattested, so no stronger route claim is made.
This validation covers one local nested-Git fixture DAG, not a persistent scheduler, cross-machine execution, production workload, or external orchestration runtime.
No third-party OpenAPI validator was installed; schema behavior is supported by direct review, generator inspection, and standard-library tests.

checks.check: nested baseline identity, exact dirty paths, and user-note hash
